analysis:
The supplied units are base-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 2792-3221), which are historical release notes. The PR itself changes only CHANGELOG.md: head adds a v0.10.7 candidate section at lines 11-413, replacing a small v0.10.6 header. The patch excerpt is truncated, so most of the new head text was not visible to me. The examined base text is documentation with no executable code, authorization logic, key handling or configuration, so no regression can be attributed to it.

I read the base excerpt against the relevant threat definitions, mainly T-041 (prefix cache, SEC-035), and it matches them. It mentions the 30-minute SSD TTL, the 750 GB/day write budget, the cache routing salt, and App Attest serving protocol 3 only. Those entries describe past behavior and do not alter any control. The 750 GB/day SSD write-budget raise (base line 2806) and the 30-minute TTL (line 2891) are documented as already shipped, and the cache-posture text in T-041 does not cover the write budget. That is pre-existing and not caused by this PR.

The head-side content cannot be assessed from this input. The v0.10.7 section describes tensor-parallel pair clustering for Gemma 4 and MiMo (#1706, #1707, #1715, #1727, #1736). It also describes a coordinated pair self-update (#1702) and a fail-closed pairing mismatch. These would touch the provider-to-provider trust boundary, update authority (T-043) and the TB-002 wire. If the actual PR includes source changes in other batches, the next pass should check pair authentication, update-path integrity and any new peer transport against the threat model, since the model has no cluster boundary. I do not claim a finding here. Because the head text was not reviewed, I recommend deeper review of the unseen content.
